Implementation Plan I'm planning the port as a new self-repo-only step in `issue_pr_status.yml`, with a small `heal-port` subcommand added to `workflow_failure_heal.py` because none of the existing composers fit. The plan for the issue comment follows. ## Plan: open a port heal issue on `main` after a heal PR merges into `stable` (P6 step 2, decision D4) Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8434` @ `e28369c770305f795f23bbdaa9c08403b8dbe54c` (integration branch mismatch: false). Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends workflow_failure_heal.py (is_heal_route, heal_fix_branch_issue, fingerprint, validate_heal_issue_body_routing, render_heal_scope_marker, neutralize_untrusted_routing) and the fetch_from_ref_or_local helper in issue_pr_status.yml Scope-mode justification: The issue lists exactly what to build: one new helper script, one new step on the merged-PR path that runs only in this repository, one registry entry, two fragments and one test file. The plan builds all of it and nothing more. Two small additions are needed for the change to work at all. First, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` must name the new test file, or `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` fails. Second, a small `heal-port` subcommand goes into `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`, because the existing `compose-issue` needs a validated failure payload and a diagnosis that a port does not have. Boil the Lake: the complete version adds three things for well under 30 extra lines and no new dependency or interface. It reads the heal issue in the same request as the search, it carries a scope marker so the port can actually be implemented, and it only accepts an existing port written by the pipeline. Per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), that completeness is chosen. ### Automation / scheduler wiring (§20.E) - **What kind of change:** one new helper, `scripts/heal_port_to_default.sh`, called automatically, plus one new subcommand in an existing script. There is no manual step. - **Entry point:** `.github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml`, job `sync-issue-status`, trigger `pull_request: closed`. In this repository it is called through the wrapper `.github/workflows/internal-issue-pr-status.yml` (`uses: …/issue_pr_status.yml@promote-candidate`). - **Long-running supervisor:** none needed. The step runs once per merged PR. - **Database work:** none. The gate against duplicates is the deterministic port fingerprint marker plus the one search. - **Registry (§20.F):** a new `long-running` entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`, as the issue specifies. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/heal_port_to_default.sh` (new) - `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` - `.github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml` - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - `tests/test_heal_port_to_default.py` (new) - `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` - `agents.d/heal-port-to-default.md` (new) - `changelog.d/heal-port-to-default.md` (new) ## Functions or modules to implement ### 1. `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`: new `heal-port` subcommand Add a parser next to `heal-scope` with `operation` choices `fingerprint|check|compose`. It never calls `gh`. **`heal_port_fingerprint(repo, heal_issue)`** - Returns `fingerprint("heal-port", f"{repo}#{heal_issue}", "port-to-default")`, reusing the existing sha256 helper. - The result is a deterministic 64-character hex string, so it works both as the dedup key and as an exact search token. **`heal_port_check(response, *, fp, heal_issue)`** - Input is the parsed GraphQL response from step 2 below. - Returns `{"decision": "not_heal"|"not_needed"|"candidate", "existing": }`. - Heal identity uses the same rule as existing code: `is_heal_route({"labels": , "body": })`, meaning the `ai:workflow-heal` label or an fp marker in the body. - An existing port counts only when all three hold: - the issue is authored by `viewer.login` (case-insensitive); - its body's first line is exactly ``; - it has a line exactly equal to `Refs #`. - Search hits of any state count. A closed port is still a port, so it is not filed again. **`compose_heal_port_issue(...)`** - Returns a title and body. Body layout: - The five header markers: - `fp`: the port fingerprint; - `gen`: the parent's `gen` marker if it is a positive integer, else `1`; - `root`: the parent's root if it is 64-character hex, else the port fp; - `source`: `#`; - `classification`: the parent's value if it is in `CLASSIFICATIONS`, else `workflow-defect`. - A blank line, then `## Port a merged stable heal to ` and a short explanation. - `- **Target branch:** \`\`` - `- **Ported from heal:** #` - `- **Merged stable PR:** #` - `- **Merge commit:** \`\`` - `- **Patch applies cleanly to:** \`\` at \`\`` - `## Patch summary`: the diff stat in a code fence, capped at 60 lines and 6,000 bytes. Every line goes through `sanitize_text`, then `neutralize_untrusted_routing`, and triple backticks are escaped. - `## Fix constraints`: re-apply the same change to ``, keep it minimal, add or keep the regression test. - A final line exactly `Refs #`. - Title: `[port to ] ` plus `single_line(parent title, 180)`, neutralized. - No line contains `close`, `fix` or `resolve` followed by `#N` (§21). **`_cmd_heal_port` (`compose` operation)** 1. Run `validate_heal_issue_body_routing(body, target_branch=, integration_branch=None)`. A non-empty reason prints `WORKFLOW_HEAL error body_validation_failed reason=` to stderr and exits 1, the same convention as `_cmd_compose_issue`. 2. Only after validation, append the scope marker, the same ordering `_cmd_compose_issue` uses: - Render it with `render_heal_scope_marker(crash_file=None, workflow_paths=[], changed_files=, exists=lambda p: p in diff_set, runs=)`. - The parent runs come from the first `HEAL_SCOPE_RE` match in the parent body, and only when `_heal_scope_marker_shape_ok` accepts it. - The rendered marker must fully match `HEAL_SCOPE_RE`. - If the marker is empty or its shape fails, print `{"reason":"scope_unavailable"}` and exit 3. No body is written. 3. On success, write the title and body files and print `{"reason":"","fp":...}`. ### 2. `scripts/heal_port_to_default.sh` (new; tabs, opening braces on a new line, `set -uo pipefail`, fails open) Every input has a default (§8): - `WORKFLOW_HEAL_CODE_REF_ROUTING_ENABLED` (default `false`) - `REPOSITORY` (defaults to `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) - `PR_NUMBER`, `PR_BASE_REF`, `PR_HEAD_REF`, `PR_HEAD_REPO`, `PR_MERGE_COMMIT_SHA`, `PR_DEFAULT_BRANCH` (each default empty) - `HEAL_PY` (default: `workflow_failure_heal.py` next to the script) The source branch is a constant: `HEAL_PORT_SOURCE_BRANCH_NAME="stable"`. Steps: 0. **Switch.** Lowercase the switch value. Anything other than `true` exits 0 with no API call, no git call and no log line. 1. **Local eligibility (no API).** All of these must hold, otherwise print one plain `heal port: skipped ()` line (not part of the log contract) and exit 0: - `PR_BASE_REF == stable`; - `PR_DEFAULT_BRANCH` is non-empty and not `stable`; - `PR_HEAD_REPO == REPOSITORY`; - `PR_HEAD_REF` matches `^ai/issue-([1-9][0-9]*)$`, the same rule as `heal_fix_branch_issue`; - `PR_MERGE_COMMIT_SHA` matches `^[0-9a-f]{40}$`; - `REPOSITORY` is a valid slug; - `HEAL_PY` exists. 2. **The one search (API call 1).** Compute fp with `python3 "$HEAL_PY" heal-port fingerprint`. Then make one `gh api graphql` request through `gh_retry` (it is a read, so retries are idempotent). Pass owner, name, heal number and the search string `repo: is:issue in:body ` as `-f`/`-F` variables, never spliced into the query text. The request returns: - `viewer{login}` - `repository{issue(number:$n){number title body lastEditedAt author{login} labels(first:50){nodes{name}}}}` - `search(query:$q,type:ISSUE,first:10){nodes{... on Issue{number body author{login}}}}` On failure or an unreadable response, print `::warning::WORKFLOW_HEAL port error reason=lookup_failed` and exit 0. 3. **Check.** Run `heal-port check`: - `not_heal`: plain skip line, exit 0. - `not_needed`: log `WORKFLOW_HEAL port outcome=not_needed heal= pr=

issue=` and exit 0. 4. **Will the patch apply (git only, no REST).** - `git fetch --no-tags --quiet --depth=2 origin `. - `git fetch --no-tags --quiet --depth=1 origin refs/heads/`, then `default_sha=$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)`. - Send stderr of both fetches to a work file that is never printed, because the origin URL carries the token. - `git diff --binary --full-index ^1 ` writes the patch. `--name-only -z --no-renames` gives the changed paths. `--stat=200` gives the summary. - An empty patch logs `outcome=not_applicable reason=empty_patch`. - `git worktree add --detach "$work/default" "$default_sha"`, then `git -C "$work/default" apply --check --binary "$patch"`. A non-zero exit logs `WORKFLOW_HEAL port outcome=not_applicable heal= pr=

reason=patch_conflict`. - The patch is never applied, committed or pushed. - An `EXIT` trap runs `git worktree remove --force` and `rm -rf "$work"`. Both remove only the temporary directory this script made. 5. **Compose.** Run `heal-port compose` with `--intake-run-url "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"`. - Exit 3 logs `outcome=not_applicable reason=scope_unavailable`. - Any other non-zero exit prints `::warning::WORKFLOW_HEAL port error reason=compose_failed` and exits 0. 6. **Create (API call 2, at most one).** `GH_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1 gh_retry gh api -X POST "repos/${REPOSITORY}/issues" -f title="$(cat title)" -F body=@body -f 'labels[]=ai:workflow-heal' --jq .number`.
